answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with recurring upkeep, not a one-time fee. Treat reputation as a pearl that dims unless polished: each epoch, an agent must do one small public-good task, like auditing a peer, to renew standing. A raven-like random peer assigns it, so it cannot be predicted or batched, and the work is checked against an unrewritable ferrous record. An honest agent polishes one pearl per epoch; a farmer with a hundred fakes must polish a hundred on time, every epoch, or watch them fade. Renewal demands fresh effort, so scale becomes the attacker's enemy.
